stem: Which infection-prevention measure is recommended for healthcare personnel each influenza season?

options.A: Use antiviral prophylaxis throughout the entire influenza season instead of vaccination.
options.B: Wear an N95 respirator during every patient interaction regardless of symptoms or exposure.
options.C: Receive seasonal influenza vaccination unless a contraindication applies.
options.D: Wait until an influenza outbreak occurs in the facility before considering vaccination.

rationale: CDC healthcare influenza guidance identifies annual influenza vaccination as the most important measure to prevent seasonal influenza infection and states that, unless contraindicated, all people aged 6 months and older, including healthcare personnel, should be vaccinated. C is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize annual seasonal influenza vaccination as a recommended infection-prevention measure for eligible healthcare personnel.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Infection Prevention and Control Strategies for Seasonal Influenza in Healthcare Settings
source_version_date: Current CDC healthcare guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Recommendations > 1. Promote and administer seasonal influenza vaccine: annual influenza vaccination is the most important prevention measure; unless contraindicated, vaccinate all people aged 6 months and older, including healthcare personnel.
source_claim_supported: Eligible healthcare personnel should receive seasonal influenza vaccination each year unless a contraindication applies.

correction_summary: Retained the infection-prevention construct and key C, confirmed current CDC healthcare guidance and annual vaccination language, and preserved easy difficulty because the final item tests a direct prevention recommendation.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Seasonal influenza prevention for healthcare personnel
audit_findings.source_authority: CDC healthcare influenza infection-control guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-16; current ACIP recommendations continue annual influenza vaccination
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Recommendations > 1. Promote and administer seasonal influenza vaccine; NCSBN Safety/Infection printed p.8 rendered and verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the current annual-vaccination recommendation and avoids claiming universal respirator use or season-long antiviral prophylaxis.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; routine season-long antiviral prophylaxis is not a substitute for recommended annual vaccination.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; N95 use is not required for every patient interaction regardless of exposure/context.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; vaccination is recommended proactively each season, not only after an outbreak begins.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C is the routine annual HCP prevention measure described by CDC.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are infection-prevention strategies and are comparable in form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection prevention for healthcare personnel and clients.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current CDC healthcare guidance, current ACIP annual-vaccination summary, all choices, rationale, objective and NCSBN Safety/Infection mapping. C remained uniquely correct.
